take_homes: A licence or login count is not adoption. I should ask for use, meaning who actually uses it on real work, and not report seats.
A rollout plan with unnamed owners is not a plan. If nobody answers for it, it won't reach the P&L.
Before pushing a tool on someone, ask what would have to be true for them to drop their spreadsheet or colleague.

monday.move: Ask my controller how the month-end variance commentary is done today, what the current way gets right, and what would make them drop it for an agent. Then agree one small test on non-sensitive data.
monday.when: This week, before month-end close starts
monday.stop_condition: The controller cannot say what would make them switch, or the test needs finance data that IT has not approved. Then I stop and ask IT first.
monday.blocker: IT has not approved the tool for finance data.

misconception.why: Rolling out access and reporting it as adoption is the licence mistake. The module said what is missing is trust, an owner and a use that fits the person's work, so it is something we build. I'm not convinced yet, because I still haven't seen a cost or payback figure.

one_line: More honest than I expected, and the story about the redesign nobody decided on was true to life, but there wasn't one cost or payback figure all day.
